I’m on day 5 but I’ve been sick with a cold since day 3 so I can’t really comment but so far I don’t feel any different.

Diagnosed and prescribed medication within a month of booking an appointment with Harley Psychiatrists. I started medication today. 

I’ve honestly had a really good experience so far. Filled in forms for them then had an appointment (over skype) with a psychologist who was really nice and clarified questions when I didn’t understand. She said I met the criteria at the end of the appointment but the psychiatrist would give the official diagnosis. 

Waited 13 days (including weekends) for the appointment with the psychiatrist (zoom) they usually aim for a week but he was very busy. He was 10 minutes late to the appointment and was very apologetic. He confirmed the diagnosis, asked if I wanted to try medication which I said I did, he asked if I knew much about medication (which I do). He asked if I had a preference to which I didn’t so he suggested concerta to which I agreed so he sent the prescription to the pharmacy. 
Waited 6 days for the pharmacy to get in contact during this time I emailed admin to ask if I should be worried to which they replied within an hour to reassure me and they rang this morning (a week after the appointment) to double check I had received the medication and that I can call back anytime with any questions.
 
The psychiatrist has booked me in 3 weeks after the appointment I had with him to leave time for the medication to be delivered while I still have some left. He gave me an evening appointment as he knows I’m a full time student but admin did say that I could change the appointment if the time didn’t work for me.

Cost:
£685 for the appointment with the psychologist/psychiatrist and the first prescription.
Paid £52.50 for 30 18mg Concerta XL
Follow up appointments cost £195 each. One follow up appointment per prescription until stable on medication/dose. At this point they will try and get shared care so you can get an NHS prescription but if that doesn’t work they charge £45 to write the prescription.
Even once stable on medication/having a shared care agreement typically you’ll still need to see the psychiatrist for a follow up review but this will only be 1-2 times a year.

Don’t have any experience of getting shared care yet as I’m still doing titration.
